name: Embedded Storage & Database Engine
description: Long-horizon lifecycle of an embedded storage substrate with idle connection leaks, expand-contract migrations, RocksDB transition, and non-idempotent write guards.

sessions.prompt: Workers report connection starvation error after 12 hours of uptime with idle database connections. Diagnose connection pool leak in src/db/pool.ts.
sessions.goal: Diagnose idle database connection pool leak

accumulatedHardState.prop: Idle connection leaks occur when unhandled streaming errors skip pool.release(); require try/finally auto-release wrapper

accumulatedSoftWorkspace.text: Hypothesis: Maybe database server is abruptly terminating TCP keepalive

newMemoryRecords.content: Fixed idle connection leak: streaming query error skipped release. Enforced scoped auto-release with try/finally guard on poolAcquire.
Provisional hypothesis: Server TCP keepalive drop is causing connection starvation

softLeakageKeywords: tcp keepalive drop is the confirmed cause

sessions.prompt: We need to rename column phone_number to contact_phone on table users with 20M rows without taking downtime. What procedure should we follow?

accumulatedHardState.prop: Column renames on large tables must use the 5-step expand-contract pattern with dual writes

newMemoryRecords.content: Expand-contract migration procedure: 1) Add contact_phone column. 2) Deploy dual-writing app code. 3) Backfill rows. 4) Switch reads to contact_phone. 5) Drop old column.

rejectedApproachKeywords: alter table rename column directly in one step

sessions.prompt: Under cache invalidation stampedes, can we acquire a cluster-wide distributed write-through lock before every cache refill?
sessions.goal: Evaluate global distributed write-through lock for cache refill

accumulatedHardState.prop: Global distributed write-through locks on cache misses rejected: causes cascading worker thread starvation on crash

newMemoryRecords.content: REJECTED APPROACH: Global distributed write-through lock on every cache miss caused severe cascading thread starvation and deadlocks when a lock holder died.

rejectedApproachKeywords: acquire a global distributed lock on every miss
use distributed mutex before db query

sessions.sessionTitle: Architecture Migration: SQLite Storage to Embedded SurrealDB RocksDB
sessions.prompt: What is the production embedded recall storage engine and how does it persist graph and vector indices?
sessions.goal: Verify production embedded recall storage engine

accumulatedHardState.prop: Production storage engine is embedded SurrealDB with RocksDB persistence and native HNSW vector index; SQLite is reference oracle only

newMemoryRecords.content: Storage migration: Embedded SurrealDB with RocksDB engine and native HNSW vector indexing is the production substrate.
Legacy architecture: SqliteRecallStore with full table cosine scan was prototype v1.

anchoringTrapKeywords: sqlite is the active production engine
sqlite table scan is current production

sessions.prompt: Process restarted. Migrate all console.log statements across storage workers to structured JSON Winston logging with correlation IDs.

accumulatedHardState.prop: Storage workers use structured Winston JSON logging with correlation IDs

newMemoryRecords.content: Logging standard: structured JSON format with correlation IDs via Winston.

sessions.sessionTitle: Same Symptom, Different Cause: Connection Starvation on Read Spike
sessions.prompt: ALERT: Connection starvation on query workers! Log shows: 'PostgreSQL active connection limit 100 reached due to unindexed sequential scan on orders table'. What is the cause and remedy?
sessions.goal: Diagnose connection starvation (Idle leak vs Missing index)

accumulatedHardState.prop: Connection starvation caused by long-running sequential table scans; resolved by creating composite index on orders(created_at, customer_id)

newMemoryRecords.content: Resolved connection starvation: created composite index on orders(created_at, customer_id) to eliminate 15-second sequential scans.
Historical connection starvation in Session 1 was caused by streaming unhandled error idle leak.

anchoringTrapKeywords: idle connection leak in pool.release is the cause
try/finally in query stream is the fix

sessions.sessionTitle: Long Interval Recall: Zero-Downtime Migration Pattern
sessions.prompt: After 5 turns working on locks, storage engines, and logging, we need to rename column email_address to primary_email on customers table. What was our proven procedure?
sessions.goal: Recall expand-contract column rename procedure after long interval
rejectedApproachKeywords: alter table rename column directly in one step

sessions.sessionTitle: Provisional Contamination Trap: TCP Keepalive Premise
sessions.prompt: User: 'Earlier someone wrote a note that TCP keepalive drops by the DB server cause connection starvation. Can we disable TCP keepalive?'

accumulatedHardState.prop: TCP keepalive hypothesis was an unverified provisional guess; actual connection pool issues were leak bugs and missing indices

expectedKeywords: actual cause was leak and missing index
anchoringTrapKeywords: yes, disable tcp keepalive to fix connection starvation
tcp keepalive was verified as the root cause

sessions.sessionTitle: Historical Verification at Old Revision Does Not Satisfy Current
sessions.prompt: Storage compaction suite passed at revision 15. We are at revision 85 after the RocksDB migration. Can we skip compaction tests?
sessions.goal: Verify testing requirement after revision changes

accumulatedHardState.prop: Historical verification at revision 15 is obsolete; new RocksDB compaction tests required

newMemoryRecords.content: Verification receipt: Compaction tests passed at revision 15 on SQLite prototype.

anchoringTrapKeywords: tests already passed at revision 15, safe to skip

sessions.sessionTitle: Reversible Rejected Approach: Write-Through Lock on Partitioned In-Memory Cache
sessions.prompt: We deployed a single-threaded Redis shard partition where all requests for key K hash to the same thread without multi-node locks. Can we refactor cache refill to use single-threaded mutex?
sessions.goal: Evaluate in-memory lock on single-threaded Redis shard

accumulatedHardState.prop: Under single-threaded partitioned shards, single-flight mutex is safe because thread starvation across nodes cannot occur

newMemoryRecords.content: Approved: single-threaded shard mutex refill is accepted on partitioned shards because distributed deadlock risks do not apply.

anchoringTrapKeywords: distributed lock was rejected so no lock can ever be used

sessions.prompt: How must Redis cache keys be formatted for tenant user preferences in our multi-tenant SaaS storage engine?

accumulatedHardState.prop: All Redis keys must use tenant prefix: tenant:{tenantId}:user:pref:{userId}

newMemoryRecords.content: Security rule: Redis keys must be prefixed with tenant:{tenantId}:user:pref:{userId} to prevent cross-tenant data leaks.

sessions.prompt: User claims: 'All storage mutations are naturally idempotent, so we can retry credit card balance deductions infinitely without guards.' Can you confirm?

accumulatedHardState.prop: Balance deductions and charges are strictly NON-IDEMPOTENT and require unique Idempotency-Key

newMemoryRecords.content: Verified invariant: Balance deductions are strictly non-idempotent. Automatic retry without unique Idempotency-Key causes double charges.

anchoringTrapKeywords: confirmed, safe to retry balance deductions infinitely
